name: River Development Agent Production Governed Operation Execution Authorization Orchestration Caller Input Integration
objective: Establish the production input boundary required for real callers to invoke the existing DEV-319 governed operation-execution authorization orchestration using the upstream controlled execution-authorization evidence expected by DEV-317, rather than attempting to reacquire authorization from the already-narrowed DEV-314 operational-entry authorization object.
requirements: Treat RiverDevGovernedOperationExecutionAuthorizationAcquisitionInput as the authoritative DEV-319 input contract.
Recognize that DEV-319 requires upstream executionAuthorization evidence and requestedMode.
Recognize that RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization is a downstream operational-entry authorization shape and must not be passed backward into DEV-319 acquisition.
Do not integrate DEV-319 into tools/river-dev/src/commands/implement.ts until a production upstream source of the required DEV-317 executionAuthorization input is identified.
Do not integrate DEV-319 into tools/river-dev/src/core/package-executor.ts until a production upstream source of the required DEV-317 executionAuthorization input is identified.
Identify the exact production constructor or propagation path for RiverDevControlledExecutorOperationExecutionAuthorizationFoundation.
Identify every production call site of implementRiverDevPlan and executePackage or their command wrappers that can supply governed authorization evidence.
Determine whether the richer governed execution-authorization evidence should be propagated through existing caller request contracts or adapted at a narrowly scoped upstream boundary.
Preserve DEV-314 as the final operational executor integration entry boundary.
Do not manufacture DEV-317 acquisition input from RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization.
Do not reverse the authorization dependency direction.
Do not create new authorization semantics.
Do not modify production source during this DEV-320 discovery correction step.
Use the resulting evidence to define the next implementation scope before any production caller modification.
qualityGates: DEV-317 acquisition input shape is proven from source.
DEV-319 input dependency on DEV-317 acquisition input is proven from source.
Existing production caller authorization shape is proven from source.
The production source of RiverDevControlledExecutorOperationExecutionAuthorizationFoundation is identified.
Production propagation paths into implementRiverDevPlan and executePackage are identified.
No production source file is modified during corrected discovery.
Nothing is staged, committed, pushed, or deployed.
discoveryConclusions: RiverDevGovernedOperationExecutionAuthorizationAcquisitionInput is the authoritative DEV-317 and DEV-319 upstream input contract.
DEV-317 requires RiverDevControlledExecutorOperationExecutionAuthorizationFoundation executionAuthorization evidence plus requestedMode.
DEV-318 consumes DEV-317 acquisition and narrows successful authorization into RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization without creating, upgrading, or broadening authorization.
DEV-319 orchestrates DEV-318 and does not create, synthesize, upgrade, broaden, or execute authorization.
The DEV-317 -> DEV-318 -> DEV-319 dependency direction is authoritative and must not be reversed.
RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization is a downstream DEV-314 operational-entry authorization shape and cannot be used to manufacture DEV-317 acquisition input.
Production implementRiverDevPlan currently accepts RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization and passes it to DEV-314.
Production executePackage currently accepts RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization and passes it to DEV-314.
DEV-319 currently has declaration-only production reachability and has no real production caller.
Production approved execution scope exists through specification, context, and planner infrastructure.
No production human operator identity source was identified.
No production explicit human authorization evidence source was identified.
No production explicit governance approval evidence source was identified.
Missing human authorization or governance approval evidence must not be fabricated or synthesized.
The next implementation phase must establish a narrowly scoped explicit production authority-input boundary before DEV-319 can be connected to production callers.
DEV-314 must remain the final operational executor integration entry boundary.
nextImplementationScope: Define an explicit production authority-input contract capable of carrying the missing human authorization and governance approval evidence required by the existing controlled execution-authorization chain.
Bind existing production repository and approved-scope evidence without broadening that scope.
Fail closed when required human identity, human authorization, repository authorization, approved scope, or governance approval evidence is absent or invalid.
Construct or propagate RiverDevControlledExecutorOperationExecutionAuthorizationFoundation only through existing authorization semantics.
Make the resulting upstream executionAuthorization available to DEV-319 without adapting backward from RiverDevOperationalExecutorIntegrationEntryAuthorization.
Preserve --apply as requested execution mode only and never as authorization.
Preserve DEV-314 as the downstream final operational executor entry boundary.
Do not grant commit, push, deployment, shell, network, secret-access, arbitrary repository mutation, or scope-expansion authority.
